analysis.title: China Economic Activity and Policy Tracker: Oct 23
key_insights: GS now publishes the China tracker weekly instead of less often, to follow the effect of the higher energy price supply shock on Chinese activity.

Property: 30-city primary-market transaction volume rose slightly over the past week but stayed well below the year-ago level. National Day holiday data was very low and may not be fully updated, and the different holiday timing distorts y/y comparisons.
16-city secondary-market transaction volume increased over the past week and was above the year-ago level.
NBS 70-city secondary home prices continued to edge down in September. Rental yields in large cities were largely flat in September, while the 30-year CGB yield ticked down.
Mobility: domestic passenger flights increased over the past week, the flight cancellation rate fell, and traffic congestion rose. Morning Consult consumer confidence increased.
Industry: steel demand fell over the past week while steel production was stable. Daily coal consumption in coastal provinces edged up.

Fiscal: RMB 3.82tn of local government special bonds have been issued year-to-date, nearing the year-ago level. Total government bond issuance reached RMB 9.61tn, or 81% of the annual quota set at the March Two Sessions.

Other activity: seasonally adjusted EPMI edged up in October. Official port container throughput edged up and remained well above year-ago levels. Freight volume of departing ships at 20 major ports increased.

Energy and commodities: the GS nowcast puts China oil demand at 17.1mb/d in the latest reading. Visible landed crude inventories increased. Outstanding US soybean export sales to China for 2026/27 rose in the second week of October.
Trade: rare earth magnet export volume to the EU and US rose in September, while volume to Japan edged down. The single-month FX conversion ratio for the goods trade balance was 66% in September.

Rates and FX: interbank and overnight repo rates edged down over the week. The US-China yield gap narrowed to 330bps but remains historically wide. CNY appreciated against USD and the CFETS basket, and the USDCNY fixing-implied countercyclical factor ticked up.

Policy: PBOC signalled on 19-Oct a shift to an overnight policy rate and a broader interest rate benchmark. On 21-Oct the State Council issued a note on integrating scientific and technological innovation with industrial innovation, and on 17-Oct it heard a report on the 'AI+' initiative.

Policy since mid-August leans toward easing: PBOC targeted easing measures on 29-Sep, a nationwide mortgage interest subsidy effective 1-Oct, RMB 550bn allocated from the unused local government debt quota on 9-Oct, and a final RMB 62.5bn batch of consumer trade-in funds on 30-Sep.

macro_indicators.interpretation: High-frequency nowcast of oil demand rose, relevant to crude balances. GS balances are updated every six weeks, so the nowcast is the faster read.
Issuance is well advanced against the March budget quota, which excludes later extra-budget quota.

risk_factors: Higher energy prices are a supply shock to Chinese economic activity.
Property transaction volume in the primary market remains well below year-ago levels, and NBS secondary home prices keep edging down.
National Day holiday timing and incomplete data distort y/y property comparisons.
